deck.title: Greek Syllable, Quantity, and Accent
deck.sub: How a Greek syllable is measured, and where the accent may stand

panels.h:
The Greek syllable. A Greek syllable, like a Latin one, has one vowel or diphthong at its center. ἄν-θρω-πος has three syllables, and παι-δεύ-ω has three, because αι and ευ are diphthongs, two vowels pronounced as one.

A syllable is long by nature when its vowel is long or a diphthong. η and ω are always long, and ε and ο are always short. α, ι, and υ may be long or short, and the macron in this course’s paradigms marks a long one, as in χώρᾱ. A syllable is long by position when a short vowel is followed by two consonants or by a double consonant, ζ, ξ, or ψ.

q.prompt: Which of these vowels is always long?
q.explain: η and ω are always long, and ε and ο are always short. α may be long or short, and the dictionary or the macron shows which.

panels.h:
The accents. Greek keeps quantity and adds a written accent on one of the last three syllables. The marks are the acute (´); the grave (`), which is written for an acute on the last syllable when another word follows; and the circumflex (ˆ), which stands only on a long vowel or a diphthong.

The law of limitation says that the accent cannot stand further back than the third syllable from the end, and that if the last syllable is long, it cannot stand on the antepenult. Verbs are usually recessive, that is, the accent goes as far back as that law allows: παιδεύω has its acute on the penult because the last syllable, ω, is long.

q.prompt: A circumflex can stand only on…
options: A long vowel or a diphthong
The last syllable of a word, and no other
A short vowel that carries the stress
q.explain: The circumflex is a rise and fall of pitch on one long sound, and so a short vowel cannot bear it.

panels.h:
The accent of nouns. The accent of a noun or an adjective is persistent, that is, it stays on the syllable where it stands in the nominative, as far as the law of limitation allows. ἄνθρωπος has its accent on the antepenult, but in the genitive ἀνθρώπου the last syllable is long, so the accent moves to the penult.

A long penult with the accent takes the circumflex when the last syllable is short, as in δῶρον, and the acute when the last syllable is long, as in δώρου. For the accent, final αι and οι count as short, except in the optative: ἄνθρωποι keeps its accent on the antepenult.

q.prompt: Why does ἄνθρωπος become ἀνθρώπου in the genitive?
options: The last syllable is now long, so the accent cannot stay on the antepenult
The genitive is always accented on the penult
The accent of a noun is recessive, as in verbs
The circumflex cannot stand on ω
q.explain: The accent of a noun stays where it is in the nominative as far as the law allows. The ending -ου is long, and a long last syllable keeps the accent off the antepenult.

panels.h: The breathings. A word that begins with a vowel or a diphthong takes a breathing, written over the vowel, or over the second vowel of a diphthong. The rough breathing (῾) is the sound of h, as in ὁ, and the smooth breathing (᾿) marks that the word does not begin with h, as in ἐστί. A word that begins with ρ takes the rough breathing: ῥήτωρ. A breathing is not a syllable and does not change the quantity.

q.prompt: What does the rough breathing in ὁ mark?
options: That the word begins with the sound h
That the syllable carries the accent
q.explain: The rough breathing is the sound h at the beginning of the word. The smooth breathing marks that there is no h. Neither one is an accent or a mark of length.

exercise.title: Greek Syllable, Quantity, and Accent
exercise.desc: A short set on the Greek syllable: its quantity, the three accents, the law of limitation, the accent of nouns and verbs, and the breathings.

items.q: How many syllables does this word have?
items.why: ἄν-θρω-πος has three vowels, and so three syllables.

items.q: How many syllables does this word have?
items.why: αι and ευ are diphthongs, each one sound, so the word is παι-δεύ-ω, three syllables.
η and ω are always long, and ε and ο are always short. α, ι, and υ may be either.

items.q: Which letters count as double consonants and make a short vowel before them long by position?
items.why: ζ, ξ, and ψ each stand for two consonants, so a short vowel before one of them makes a syllable long by position.

items.q: The three Greek accent marks are…
items.why: The marks show the pitch of a syllable. A circumflex stands only on a long vowel or a diphthong. The breathings are not accents.

items.q: In Greek, if the last syllable is long, the accent cannot stand on…
items.why: By the law of limitation, a long last syllable keeps the accent off the antepenult. Verbs still go as far back as the law allows.

items.q: Why does παιδεύω have its accent on the penult?
items.a: The accent of a verb is recessive, and the long last syllable stops it at the penult
ds: The penult is always accented in Greek
The diphthong ευ must carry the accent
items.why: A verb's accent goes as far back as the law allows. The last syllable, ω, is long, so the accent cannot reach the antepenult and stands on the penult.

items.q: Why does δῶρον have a circumflex and not an acute?
items.a: The accented penult is long and the last syllable is short
ds: Every noun in -ον takes the circumflex
The circumflex marks the rough breathing
items.why: A long penult that carries the accent takes the circumflex when the last syllable is short. In the genitive δώρου the last syllable is long, and the acute is written.

items.q: What happens to the accent of ἄνθρωπος in the genitive singular?
items.a: It moves to the penult, because the ending -ου is long
ds: It stays on the antepenult, because the accent of a noun never moves
It moves to the last syllable
It becomes a circumflex on the antepenult
items.why: The accent of a noun stays where it is in the nominative as far as the law allows. A long last syllable keeps it off the antepenult, so it moves to the penult.

items.q: For the accent, how is final -οι of ἄνθρωποι counted?
items.a: As short, so the accent may stay on the antepenult
ds: As long, because οι is a diphthong
As long, so the accent must move
items.why: Final αι and οι count as short for the accent, except in the optative, so ἄνθρωποι keeps the accent on the antepenult.

items.q: What does the rough breathing mark?
items.a: That the word begins with the sound h
items.why: The rough breathing is the sound h at the beginning of the word, as in ὁ. The smooth breathing marks that there is no h.

items.q: Which breathing does a word beginning with ρ take?
items.why: A word that begins with ρ takes the rough breathing, as in ῥήτωρ.

items.q: When is the grave accent written?
items.a: For an acute on the last syllable when another word follows
ds: On the antepenult of a verb
On a word that begins with a vowel
items.why: An acute on the last syllable becomes a grave when another word follows without a pause, as in τὸν ἄνθρωπον.

items.q: Why may ἄνθρωπός ἐστι have two accents on ἄνθρωπος?
items.a: ἐστι is an enclitic, and it gives the word before it a second accent
ds: Every noun before a verb takes two accents
The second accent marks the genitive
items.why: An enclitic has no accent of its own and is pronounced with the word before it. A word accented on the antepenult then takes a second accent on its last syllable.
